The physician may be liable if the cervical manipulation caused a vertebral artery dissection resulting in posterior circulation stroke, and he failed to warn the patient of this risk or recognize warning signs. Liability depends on whether the technique was performed negligently or without adequate informed consent regarding a known serious complication. The team note is incorrect: cervical osteoarthritis is not an absolute contraindication to all neck treatment, so treating this patient is not automatically a breach of the standard of care.
CONFIDENCE: 75
